newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SDP EXTENDS OPINION POLL LEAD - TV NEWS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SDP EXTENDS OPINION POLL LEAD - TV NEWS.

text.p: Finland's Social Democratic Party (SDP) extended its lead in opinion polls one month before municipal and European Parliament elections on October 20, Finnish television news reported on Sunday.

A September 15-25 poll among 1,500 Finns of voting age made on behalf of channel MTV3 by the Radar institute gave Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's SDP a rating of 26.6 percent, up 1.5 percentage points on a Radar survey one month earlier.
The second biggest party in the left-right-green government coalition, the Conservative Party, gained 1.3 percentage points to 19.6 percent, MTV3 news said.

Of the other coalition parties, the Leftist Alliance was steady at 10.5 percent, the Green Party down two percentage points at seven percent and the Swedish People's Party holding its own at 5.3 percent.
The biggest opposition grouping, the Centre Party, retreated one percentage point to 20.4 percent, MTV3 news said.

The October 20 elections will be the first real test of popular support for Finland's political parties since the March 1995 general election which brought Lipponen's rainbow alliance to power. His cabinet took over after a centre-right coalition.
